reviewType: Individual 156-question review of named source targets, model-assisted; variable/figurative traits explicitly qualified

rows.name: friendship
rows.reviewNotes: An intangible relationship, not a physical animal or object. Physical-trait questions are answered literally, not metaphorically; joy/love/usefulness are intentionally affirmative. Its figurative fragility is softened.

rows.name: mail (snail mail)
rows.reviewNotes: Postal letters and envelopes, not an actual snail or other organism. Variations in stationery size, colour and decoration use softened probabilities. Combustible refers to ordinary paper postal letters.

rows.name: love
rows.reviewNotes: An emotional attachment, not a physical object. Retains subjective love, fragility and metaphorical warmth as recorded.

rows.name: time
rows.reviewNotes: Duration is not physically observable or tangible; idiomatic passage of time and longstanding use are retained.

rows.name: sleep
rows.reviewNotes: Sleep is a physiological state and experience, not a tangible physical object; abstract/conceptual classification corrected.

rows.name: a dream
rows.reviewNotes: A dream is an experience during sleep, not a physical thing, and is classified as an abstract experience.

rows.name: magic
rows.reviewNotes: Interpret magic as the concept or practice, not a living organism or physical animal. Retain age, art and games links; reject biological and physical traits.

rows.name: a joke
rows.reviewNotes: A joke communicates and may be heard or written, but is not a living organism or physical object in its own right.

rows.name: a poem
rows.reviewNotes: A poem is the composition, not a particular physical printed sheet. Poetry is intangible as a work but can be read or sold on paper.

rows.name: a song
rows.reviewNotes: A song is a musical composition/performance rather than a tangible object; distinct from a recording medium.

rows.name: a smile
rows.reviewNotes: A smile is an observable facial expression, not an independently touchable physical object.

rows.name: a kiss
rows.reviewNotes: A kiss is a human action and may be pleasurable, but is not universally addictive.

rows.name: a novel
rows.reviewNotes: Refers to a physical published book, consistent with source questions about size, holding, manufacturing and recycling.

rows.name: a movie
rows.reviewNotes: Motion pictures were publicly screened by 1895, so existed more than a century before 2026; songs about films exist but are not universal. https://www.history.com/this-day-in-history/december-28/first-commercial-movie-screened

rows.name: a game
rows.reviewNotes: A physical game or play experience can be useful and some games become addictive, but both are variable, not universal.

rows.name: a number
rows.reviewNotes: A number is an abstract mathematical entity, not literally smaller than bread; numerals are visible but numbers are not physical objects.

rows.name: money
rows.reviewNotes: Green is common for some currency notes, but not a universal trait, especially across currencies; soften its colour.

rows.name: a burp
rows.reviewNotes: A burp may be heard and smelled; the sound or air release itself is not normally visible.

rows.name: a fart
rows.reviewNotes: A bodily gas emission can be smelled and heard; variability in visibility and bodily sensation is handled by existing softened responses.

rows.name: the color blue
rows.reviewNotes: Blue is an observable colour/property; it may be described as a concept in an abstract question, but is not itself an object.

rows.name: the color red
rows.reviewNotes: Red is an observable colour/property; abstract classification is softened because it can be visually experienced.

rows.name: the color green
rows.reviewNotes: Green is an observable colour/property; abstract classification is softened because it can be visually experienced.

rows.name: happiness
rows.reviewNotes: Happiness is an emotion whose expression may be observed in people, but it is not a tangible object.

rows.name: the wind
rows.reviewNotes: Wind may be cold or warm depending on conditions; cold cannot be universally Yes.
